preamble: A palatalized [sʲ], or an [s] fused with a following [j], can shift its primary constriction back to the postalveolar region and become [ʃ]. In Goidelic, the slender (palatalized) partner of broad /sˠ/ is realized as postalveolar [ʃ]. In English, yod-coalescence turned /sj/ into [ʃ] in words such as issue and pressure.

examples.from: slender s (palatalized counterpart of broad /sˠ/; Old Irish /sʲ/)
examples.note: The slender fricative of the palatalized series is typically postalveolar [ʃ]; Old Irish /sʲ/ is thought to have had the same or a similar [ɕ ~ ʃ] value.
Yod-coalescence of /sj/ to [ʃ]; the intermediate form [ˈɪʃjuː] is also common. The same change gave [ʃ] in words ending in -ssure such as pressure.

sources: Wikipedia. Phonological history of English consonant clusters (Yod-coalescence). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_English_consonant_clusters
